option_a: 'I shall reduce all your taxes by fifty percent immediately'
option_b: 'I will abdicate the throne and make Jeroboam king'
option_c: 'Let us unite to build a massive new palace in Ephraim'
option_d: 'My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions'
explanation: Rejecting the wise counsel of the elders, Rehoboam followed the harsh advice of his young peers, sparking the ten northern tribes to rebel.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: Following the division of the kingdom around 931 BC, who became the first king of the Northern Kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 12:20)?
option_a: Jeroboam, the son of Nebat
option_b: Rehoboam, the son of Solomon
option_c: Ahab, the son of Omri
option_d: Jehu, the son of Nimshi
explanation: Ten northern tribes broke away under Jeroboam I (Northern Kingdom of Israel), leaving only Judah and Benjamin to Rehoboam (Southern Kingdom of Judah).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What notorious sin did Jeroboam I commit to prevent his northern subjects from travelling to Jerusalem to worship (1 Kings 12:28-30)?
option_a: He built a wall of iron across the border of Judah
option_b: He fashioned two golden calves, setting one in Bethel and the other in Dan, leading Israel into institutional idolatry
option_c: He forced all citizens to speak the Phoenician language
option_d: He executed all descendants of the house of David
explanation: Jeroboam set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel, saying 'Behold your gods, O Israel', creating state-sponsored idolatry that corrupted the North.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: Who was the wicked Phoenician princess who married King Ahab of Israel and introduced the state worship of Baal and Asherah (1 Kings 16:31)?
option_a: Athaliah
option_b: Delilah
option_c: Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians
option_d: Vashti
explanation: Jezebel brought rampant Baal worship, murdered the prophets of the Lord, and sought to exterminate the worship of Yahweh in Israel.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What dramatic drought prophecy did the prophet Elijah the Tishbite proclaim before King Ahab in 1 Kings 17:1?
option_a: 'The River Jordan shall overflow its banks for seven months'
option_b: 'A swarm of locusts will darken the sun for forty days'
option_c: 'An earthquake will destroy the royal palace in Samaria'
option_d: 'As the Lord the God of Israel lives... there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word'
explanation: Elijah challenged the fertility god Baal by decreeing a three-and-a-half-year drought: there would be neither dew nor rain except by his prophetic word.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: How was Elijah miraculously sustained during the first part of the drought at the brook Cherith (1 Kings 17:2-6)?
option_a: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he drank from the brook
option_b: Angels dropped baskets of fruit from the clouds daily
option_c: The local villagers sent him sheep and milk secretly
option_d: He ate honey and wild locusts found in the rocks
explanation: God commanded ravens to bring Elijah bread and meat morning and evening, while the brook Cherith provided drinking water.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What miracle of multiplication did Elijah perform for the destitute widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:14-16)?
option_a: Her barren olive trees bore fresh fruit overnight
option_b: Her jar of flour was not spent and her cruse of oil did not fail until the day the Lord sent rain upon the earth
option_c: Her copper coins transformed into solid gold shekels
option_d: Her empty water cistern was filled with sweet milk
explanation: Because she baked a small cake for Elijah first, God multiplied her flour and oil throughout the remaining famine.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What climactic contest between Yahweh and Baal took place on Mount Carmel in 1 Kings 18?
option_a: A military duel between Elijah and the royal army of Samaria
option_b: A theatrical poetry recitation contest before King Ahab
option_c: Elijah confronted 450 prophets of Baal to see which God would answer by consuming the sacrifice with fire from heaven
option_d: An agricultural plowing race using twelve yoke of oxen
explanation: Elijah challenged Baal's prophets on Mount Carmel: 'The God who answers by fire, he is God.' Fire fell from heaven and consumed Elijah's water-soaked altar.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What crime did Jezebel engineer against Naboth the Jezreelite on behalf of King Ahab in 1 Kings 21?
option_a: She poisoned Naboth's wells with toxic snake venom
option_b: She banished Naboth to the desert of Damascus
option_c: She stole Naboth's prize cattle during midnight
option_d: She hired false witnesses (sons of Belial) to accuse Naboth of blasphemy, having him stoned to death to seize his ancestral vineyard
explanation: When Naboth refused to sell his ancestral vineyard, Jezebel arranged a mock trial with false accusers who had Naboth stoned to death so Ahab could steal the land.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: How was the prophet Elijah taken up into heaven at the end of his earthly ministry in 2 Kings 2:11?
option_a: A chariot of fire and horses of fire separated him from Elisha, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven
option_b: He died of old age and was buried on Mount Carmel
option_c: He was killed in battle by Syrian chariot forces
option_d: He was carried across the river Jordan by desert ravens
explanation: Elijah did not experience physical death; a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared, and Elijah ascended to heaven in a whirlwind.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: What dying request did Elisha make of Elijah before Elijah was taken up into heaven (2 Kings 2:9)?
option_a: 'Give me your golden signet ring and staff'
option_b: 'Let me inherit a double portion of your spirit'
option_c: 'Strike King Ahab with sudden blindness'
option_d: 'Crown me as the supreme prophet in Samaria'
explanation: Elisha asked for the double portion belonging to the firstborn spiritual heir, inheriting Elijah's mantle and performing twice as many recorded miracles.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Division of the Kingdom & Religious Reforms (Elijah, Elisha)
question: How was Naaman, the commander of the Syrian army, miraculously healed of his incurable leprosy through Elisha's instructions (2 Kings 5)?
option_a: He drank a secret herbal concoction brewed by Elisha
option_b: He offered ten talents of silver at the altar of Bethel
option_c: He dipped himself seven times in the River Jordan in obedient faith
option_d: He bathed in the rivers of Damascus (Abana and Pharpar)
explanation: Humbling his pride, Naaman washed seven times in the muddy Jordan River; his flesh was restored like that of a clean little child.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What magnificent vision of God's holiness accompanied Isaiah's prophetic call in the year that King Uzziah died (Isaiah 6:1-8)?
option_a: He saw a valley of dry bones coming back to life
option_b: He saw a great whirlwind carrying a chariot of fire
option_c: He saw four horns scattered by four blacksmiths
option_d: He saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and seraphim crying: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts'
explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord enthroned in the temple with seraphim chanting His holiness; a live coal touched his lips, purifying him for his mission ('Here am I! Send me').
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: Which famous messianic prophecy regarding the virgin birth was delivered by Isaiah to King Ahaz in Isaiah 7:14?
option_a: 'Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel'
option_b: 'A star shall come forth out of Jacob, and a scepter out of Israel'
option_c: 'He shall be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah, little among the clans of Judah'
option_d: 'Out of Egypt have I called my firstborn son'
explanation: Isaiah 7:14 proclaims the messianic sign: 'Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel' ('God with us').
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What central theme characterizes the fourth Servant Song of Isaiah in Isaiah 52:13 - 53:12?
option_a: The military conquest of Babylonian chariot forces by King Cyrus
option_b: The Suffering Servant who bears our griefs, is wounded for our transgressions, and makes intercession for the transgressors
option_c: The rebuilding of the marble walls of Jerusalem by Nehemiah
option_d: The joyful return of agricultural prosperity to Mount Zion
explanation: Isaiah 53 is the supreme prophecy of the vicarious, substitutionary atonement of Christ: 'He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities...'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: Why did young Jeremiah initially object when God called him to be a prophet to the nations (Jeremiah 1:4-10)?
option_a: He claimed he was too old and blind to travel
option_b: He refused because his family worshipped the god Baal
option_c: He protested: 'Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth'
option_d: He said he was already serving as high priest in Jerusalem
explanation: Jeremiah pleaded youth and lack of eloquence; God touched his mouth, saying: 'Do not say, I am only a youth... for I have put my words in your mouth.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What revolutionary spiritual promise did Jeremiah proclaim in Jeremiah 31:31-34 regarding the 'New Covenant'?
option_a: God will rebuild the temple of Solomon twice as large with solid gold
option_b: Israel will be given permanent military dominion over all world empires
option_c: Burnt animal offerings will be doubled in the courts of Jerusalem
option_d: God will write His law upon their hearts, forgive their iniquity, and they shall all know Him from the least to the greatest
explanation: Jeremiah prophesied the New Covenant: internal transformation where God inscribes His law on the human heart, granting personal knowledge and complete pardon.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What did the wicked King Jehoiakim do when Jehudi read Jeremiah's prophetic scroll to him in Jeremiah 36:20-26?
option_a: He cut it with a penknife and tossed it piece by piece into the hearth fire until the entire scroll was consumed
option_b: He wept in deep repentance and tore his royal robes
option_c: He ordered the scroll preserved in the holy of holies
option_d: He gave Jeremiah half of the royal palace treasury
explanation: In brazen defiance, Jehoiakim cut the scroll with a clerk's knife and burned it in the fireplace; God commanded Jeremiah to dictate an expanded scroll.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What was the central social and religious message of the prophet Amos at Bethel (Amos 5:21-24)?
option_a: God demands that Israel offer more fat bullocks and sweet wine
option_b: God despises hypocritical, hollow religious rituals and demands that justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream
option_c: Israel must form a military alliance with Egypt against Assyria
option_d: Only the wealthy merchant class will enter the kingdom of God
explanation: Amos blasted social oppression, corruption, and hollow ceremonialism, calling for social justice: 'Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: How did Amos satirize the luxury-obsessed, self-indulgent aristocratic women of Samaria in Amos 4:1?
option_a: He praised them as lovely gazelles of the valley
option_b: He commended their dedication to household embroidery
option_c: He called them 'Cows of Bashan' who oppress the poor, crush the needy, and demand wine from their husbands
option_d: He called them faithful daughters of Queen Sarah
explanation: Amos sharply rebuked the pampered wealthy women of Samaria as 'kine (cows) of Bashan' for oppressing the poor and fueling luxurious self-indulgence.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What personal domestic tragedy did the prophet Hosea experience that God used as an allegory of Israel's unfaithfulness (Hosea 1-3)?
option_a: His wife and three sons were killed by a Philistine army
option_b: His home in Samaria was destroyed by a massive earthquake
option_c: His wife abandoned him to enter a pagan temple as priestess
option_d: God commanded him to marry Gomer, a promiscuous woman who committed adultery, illustrating Israel's spiritual whoredom against Yahweh
explanation: Hosea's marriage to wayward Gomer mirrored God's covenant relationship with unfaithful Israel, demonstrating relentless divine love pursuing an adulterous spouse.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: What famous declaration in Hosea 6:6 highlights the primacy of inward love over outward animal sacrifices?
option_a: 'For I desire steadfast love (mercy) and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God, rather than burnt offerings'
option_b: 'Bring no more vain oblations into my holy courts'
option_c: 'The Lord delights in the smell of burning fat portions'
option_d: 'Whoever offers a bullock shall inherit the kingdom'
explanation: Hosea 6:6 emphasizes covenant loyalty (chesed): 'For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God, rather than burnt offerings' (quoted by Jesus in Matthew 9:13).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: Which imperial superpower besieged and conquered Samaria in 722 BC, deporting the ten northern tribes into exile?
option_a: Babylon (under Nebuchadnezzar)
option_b: Assyria (under Shalmaneser V and Sargon II)
option_c: Persia (under Cyrus the Great)
option_d: Rome (under Julius Caesar)
explanation: The Assyrian Empire conquered Samaria in 722 BC, bringing an end to the Northern Kingdom of Israel and deporting its population into exile.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: The Writing Prophets: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Hosea
question: Which Babylonian monarch besieged and destroyed Jerusalem, burning the Temple of Solomon in 586 BC (2 Kings 25)?
option_a: Sennacherib
option_b: Tiglath-Pileser III
option_c: Nebuchadnezzar II
option_d: Belshazzar
explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and Solomon's temple in 586 BC, carrying Judah into the Babylonian Exile.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: In Ezekiel 37:1-14, what profound vision did God show the prophet Ezekiel in the Babylonian exile?
option_a: A golden chariot riding across the river Chebar
option_b: A vision of the New Jerusalem descending from heaven
option_c: A tree reaching to the sky cut down by a holy watcher
option_d: A valley full of dry human bones which, when prophesied to, came together, were clothed with flesh, breathed on by the Spirit, and stood up as an exceedingly great army
explanation: The Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones symbolizes the national, spiritual resurrection and restoration of hopeless, exiled Israel by God's Spirit.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: In Ezekiel 33:1-9, what solemn responsibility did God assign to Ezekiel as a spiritual 'Watchman' over the house of Israel?
option_a: To warn the wicked of impending judgment; if he warns them and they refuse to repent, their blood is on their own heads, but if he fails to warn them, their blood is required at his hand
option_b: To command the military guards at the city gates of Babylon
option_c: To guard the royal treasures of King Nebuchadnezzar
option_d: To predict the exact day the sun would experience an eclipse
explanation: As a watchman, Ezekiel was accountable for faithfully blowing the trumpet to warn the people; silence would bring personal guilt for their deaths.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: In Ezekiel 18, what false proverb ('The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge') did God overturn?
option_a: The belief that agricultural grape harvests should be taxed by kings
option_b: The belief in collective hereditary guilt, declaring instead that 'the soul that sins shall die; the son shall not suffer for the iniquity of the father'
option_c: The tradition of eating unwashed fruit before morning prayers
option_d: The doctrine that elderly elders possess superior tooth strength
explanation: Ezekiel 18 establishes personal moral responsibility: each individual is judged on their own righteousness or wickedness, not on ancestral sins.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Which Persian king issued the famous 538 BC imperial decree allowing the Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple of God (Ezra 1:1-4)?
option_a: Darius the Mede
option_b: Artaxerxes I
option_c: Cyrus the Great
option_d: Xerxes (Ahasuerus)
explanation: In 538 BC, King Cyrus of Persia issued his historic edict fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy, authorizing the Jewish exiles under Zerubbabel to return and rebuild the Temple.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Who led the first wave of Jewish returnees from Babylon to Jerusalem to lay the foundation of the Second Temple (Ezra 2-3)?
option_a: Ezra the scribe
option_b: Nehemiah the cupbearer
option_c: Daniel the statesman
option_d: Zerubbabel (the governor) and Jeshua (the high priest)
explanation: Zerubbabel (descendant of David) and Jeshua (high priest) led the initial returnees in 537 BC and rebuilt the altar and temple foundations.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Which two post-exilic prophets inspired, rebuked, and encouraged the discouraged returnees to resume and finish rebuilding the Temple (Ezra 5:1-2)?
option_a: Haggai and Zechariah
option_b: Malachi and Obadiah
option_c: Joel and Habakkuk
option_d: Jonah and Nahum
explanation: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews, overcoming political opposition and apathy, leading to the completion of the Second Temple in 516 BC.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Who was Ezra in the post-exilic restoration community (Ezra 7:1-10)?
option_a: A military general who commanded Persian cavalry units
option_b: A skilled scribe and priest dedicated to studying, doing, and teaching the Law of the Lord in Israel
option_c: A master stone mason who carved the temple pillars
option_d: The Persian royal treasurer in charge of provincial taxes
explanation: Ezra was a priest and scribe who set his heart to study the Law of the Lord, obey it, and teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: What major spiritual crisis did Ezra confront and resolve among the returned Jewish community in Ezra 9-10?
option_a: The total refusal of farmers to plant agricultural crops
option_b: A military mutiny against the Persian royal governor
option_c: The widespread problem of intermarriage with pagan, idolatrous surrounding peoples, leading the people to repent and separate
option_d: A strike conducted by the Levitical singers at the temple
explanation: Ezra mourned in sackcloth over the community's unfaithfulness in marrying pagan Canaanite wives, leading a corporate covenant renewal to put away foreign idols.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: What high, trusted official office did Nehemiah hold in the Persian court at Susa before returning to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 1:11)?
option_a: Chief of the royal palace guards
option_b: Master of the royal treasury mint
option_c: Chief astrologer of the Persian court
option_d: Cupbearer to King Artaxerxes
explanation: Nehemiah was cupbearer to Artaxerxes I, a position of immense trust, access, and political influence in the imperial court.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: What devastating news brought by Hanani regarding Jerusalem moved Nehemiah to weep, fast, and pray in Nehemiah 1:1-4?
option_a: The survivors in the province were in great trouble and shame, the wall of Jerusalem was broken down, and its gates destroyed by fire
option_b: The Second Temple had been demolished by the Samaritan army
option_c: A deadly plague had wiped out all the livestock in Judah
option_d: The Persian king had rescinded the decree of return
explanation: Hearing that Jerusalem lay defenseless with broken walls and burned gates, Nehemiah fasted and interceded before the God of heaven.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Who were the primary conspiratorial adversaries who ridiculed, threatened, and plotted to halt Nehemiah's rebuilding of the walls (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:1-8)?
option_a: Pharaoh and his chariot commanders
option_b: Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arab
option_c: Haman the Agagite and his sons
option_d: Hophni and Phinehas
explanation: Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem used mockery, intimidation, false rumors, and armed threats to stop the reconstruction of Jerusalem's defensive perimeter.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

topic: Exile & Return: Ezekiel, Nehemiah, Ezra
question: Through prayer, vigilant armed shifts, and extraordinary leadership, in how many days did Nehemiah and the people complete the rebuilding of the wall (Nehemiah 6:15)?
option_a: In forty days
option_b: In one hundred and twenty days
option_c: In exactly fifty-two (52) days
option_d: In seven days
explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 records the astonishing architectural and military feat: 'So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ

question: Which angel appeared to the Virgin Mary in Nazareth to announce that she would conceive the Son of God (Luke 1:26-38)?
option_a: Angel Michael
option_b: Angel Raphael
option_c: Angel Uriel
option_d: Angel Gabriel
explanation: In Luke 1:26, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to Joseph named Mary.
