section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: What joyful event occurred when pregnant Mary greeted her relative Elizabeth in the hill country of Judah (Luke 1:39-45)?
option_a: The baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit
option_b: Elizabeth was struck mute until the child was born
option_c: An earthquake shook the house of Zechariah
option_d: Three angels appeared with golden harps
explanation: When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the unborn child (John the Baptist) leaped in her womb, and she proclaimed Mary blessed among women.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: Mary's famous song of praise in Luke 1:46-55 beginning 'My soul magnifies the Lord' is known in Christian liturgy as the:
option_a: Benedictus
option_b: Magnificat
option_c: Nunc Dimittis
option_d: Gloria in Excelsis Deo
explanation: The Magnificat (Latin for '[My soul] magnifies') is Mary's hymn celebrating God's mercy, faithfulness, and exaltation of the humble.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: Why did Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem in Judea just before Jesus was born (Luke 2:1-5)?
option_a: To escape a military invasion by the Syrian army
option_b: To sell their carpentry workshop in Bethlehem
option_c: To be enrolled (registered) in a census decreed by Caesar Augustus, because Joseph was of the house and lineage of David
option_d: To attend the annual Feast of Tabernacles in the temple
explanation: Caesar Augustus decreed a worldwide census; because Joseph belonged to the house of David, he had to register in David's ancestral town of Bethlehem.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: To whom was the birth of Jesus first announced by an angel accompanied by a heavenly host praising God (Luke 2:8-14)?
option_a: The chief priests and scribes in the Jerusalem Temple
option_b: King Herod the Great in his royal palace
option_c: The Roman governor Pontius Pilate
option_d: Shepherds keeping watch over their flock by night in the fields near Bethlehem
explanation: An angel of the Lord appeared to humble shepherds in the fields of Bethlehem, announcing 'good tidings of great joy' for all people.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: What symbolic gifts did the Wise Men (Magi) from the East present to the child Jesus in Matthew 2:11?
option_a: Gold, Frankincense, and Myrrh
option_b: Silver, Bronze, and Iron
option_c: Wheat, Olive Oil, and Honey
option_d: A crown of pearls, a royal purple robe, and a sceptre
explanation: The Magi offered Gold (symbolizing royalty/kingship), Frankincense (symbolizing divinity/priesthood), and Myrrh (symbolizing mortality/sacrificial death).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: Why did an angel instruct Joseph in a dream to take young Jesus and His mother and flee to Egypt (Matthew 2:13-15)?
option_a: Because a severe drought had struck the land of Judea
option_b: Because King Herod was about to search for the young child to destroy Him (Massacre of the Innocents)
option_c: Because Joseph had received a job offer as palace architect in Alexandria
option_d: To fulfill a vow made by Zechariah in the temple
explanation: God warned Joseph of Herod's murderous jealousy, prompting the flight to Egypt until Herod's death, fulfilling: 'Out of Egypt have I called my son'.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: Who was the devout, righteous elderly man in the Jerusalem Temple who took infant Jesus in his arms and proclaimed the Nunc Dimittis (Luke 2:25-35)?
option_a: Zechariah
option_b: Nicodemus
option_c: Simeon
option_d: Gamaliel
explanation: Simeon had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before seeing the Lord's Christ; he praised God: 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace...'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: Who was the eighty-four-year-old prophetess who served God with fastings and prayers night and day, praising God when she saw infant Jesus (Luke 2:36-38)?
option_a: Deborah
option_b: Huldah
option_c: Priscilla
option_d: Anna, daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher
explanation: Anna the prophetess gave thanks to God and spoke of the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: At twelve years of age, where did Joseph and Mary find Jesus after searching for Him for three days in Jerusalem (Luke 2:41-50)?
option_a: In the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions
option_b: Walking beside the waters of the Pool of Siloam
option_c: In the marketplace buying bread for traveling pilgrims
option_d: Outside the city walls on the Mount of Olives
explanation: They found twelve-year-old Jesus in the Temple, astonishing scholars with His understanding; Jesus asked: 'Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: According to Luke 2:52, in what four aspects did young Jesus grow during His formative childhood years in Nazareth?
option_a: In martial strength, political ambition, eloquence, and gold wealth
option_b: In wisdom (intellectual), in stature (physical), and in favor with God (spiritual) and man (social)
option_c: In military tactics, Greek philosophy, Latin law, and sailing
option_d: In miraculous power, royal authority, physical isolation, and silence
explanation: Luke 2:52 outlines balanced holistic human development: 'And Jesus increased in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and man.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Birth, Childhood & Preparation of Jesus
question: What was John the Baptist's primary prophetic message preaching in the wilderness of Judea (Matthew 3:1-2)?
option_a: 'Build new stone synogogues across Galilee'
option_b: 'Pay your taxes promptly to the Roman emperor'
option_c: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand'
option_d: 'Fast for seventy days to earn angelic wings'
explanation: John was the voice crying in the wilderness preparing the way of the Lord, proclaiming a baptism of repentance: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: Why did Jesus insist on being baptized by John in the River Jordan, despite John's protestations (Matthew 3:13-15)?
option_a: Because Jesus needed to confess personal sins of youth
option_b: To prove that He was physically capable of swimming in the Jordan
option_c: To comply with an executive order issued by King Herod Antipas
option_d: To fulfill all righteousness and identify completely with sinful humanity
explanation: Jesus had no sin, but said: 'Let it be so now; for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness', inaugurating His public messianic ministry.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: What supernatural events accompanied the baptism of Jesus as He came up out of the water (Matthew 3:16-17)?
option_a: The heavens opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven said: 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased'
option_b: An earthquake shook the hills and the river Jordan stopped flowing
option_c: Twelve angels descended and placed a golden crown on Jesus' head
option_d: The sun was darkened for three hours over Judea
explanation: All three persons of the Trinity were manifested: the Son baptized, the Spirit descending like a dove, and the Father speaking from heaven.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: For how long did Jesus fast in the Judean wilderness before being tempted by the Devil (Matthew 4:1-2)?
option_a: Seven days and seven nights
option_b: Forty days and forty nights
option_c: Twelve days and nights
option_d: One hundred days
explanation: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights in the desert, echoing Israel's forty years in the wilderness and Moses' forty days on Sinai.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: In the first temptation (Matthew 4:3-4), what did the tempter urge Jesus to do, and how did Jesus answer?
option_a: Turn water into sweet wine; Jesus replied: 'My hour has not yet come'
option_b: Steal bread from the temple; Jesus replied: 'Thou shalt not steal'
option_c: Command stones to become loaves of bread; Jesus replied: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'
option_d: Plant wheat in the desert; Jesus replied: 'The harvest is past'
explanation: Satan tempted Him to satisfy physical hunger independently of God; Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 8:3, asserting that spiritual obedience supersedes physical appetite.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: In the second temptation according to Matthew 4:5-7, the devil took Jesus to the pinnacle of the Temple and challenged Him to:
option_a: Burn the altar of incense; Jesus answered: 'The temple is holy'
option_b: Pronounce a curse on the Roman soldiers; Jesus answered: 'Love your enemies'
option_c: Demand gold from the temple treasury; Jesus answered: 'Give to Caesar what is Caesar's'
option_d: Throw Himself down, quoting Scripture; Jesus answered: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God'
explanation: Satan misquoted Psalm 91 to incite sensational presumption; Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:16: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: In the third temptation (Matthew 4:8-10), the devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and offered them if Jesus would:
option_a: Fall down and worship him; Jesus answered: 'Begone, Satan! for it is written, You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve'
option_b: Lead a violent military revolt against Rome; Jesus answered: 'Put away your sword'
option_c: Eat forbidden fruit from the tree of life; Jesus answered: 'I am the bread of life'
option_d: Sign a treaty of alliance; Jesus answered: 'No man can serve two masters'
explanation: Satan offered a shortcut to earthly dominion without the suffering of the Cross; Jesus rebuked him with Deuteronomy 6:13, commanding exclusive worship of God.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: Which two fisherman brothers casting a net into the Sea of Galilee were the first called by Jesus with the words 'Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men' (Matthew 4:18-20)?
option_a: James and John, sons of Zebedee
option_b: Simon (Peter) and Andrew
option_c: Philip and Bartholomew
option_d: Thomas and Matthew
explanation: Jesus called the brothers Simon Peter and Andrew beside the Sea of Galilee, challenging them to become fishers of men; they immediately left their nets.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: Which other two brothers, sons of Zebedee, were mending their nets in a boat with their father when Jesus called them (Matthew 4:21-22)?
option_a: Philip and Thomas
option_b: Simon and Jude
option_c: James and John
option_d: Matthew and Thaddaeus
explanation: James and John, the sons of Zebedee (nicknamed 'Boanerges' / Sons of Thunder), left their boat, hired servants, and father to follow Christ.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: What was Matthew's (Levi's) profession before he abandoned his booth to follow Jesus (Matthew 9:9)?
option_a: Fisherman on the Lake of Gennesaret
option_b: Tentmaker in Corinth
option_c: Pharisee scribe in the Sanhedrin
option_d: Tax collector (Publican)
explanation: Matthew was sitting at the tax collector's booth in Capernaum when Jesus called him; he rose, left all, and held a great feast in his house for Jesus.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: What skeptical question did Nathanael ask Philip when Philip announced that they had found the Messiah, Jesus of Nazareth (John 1:45-46)?
option_a: 'Can anything good come out of Nazareth?'
option_b: 'Is he not the son of a Roman soldier?'
option_c: 'Has he studied under Rabbi Hillel?'
option_d: 'Where are his golden chariot horses?'
explanation: Nathanael expressed regional prejudice: 'Can anything good come out of Nazareth?' Philip answered with the timeless invitation: 'Come and see.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: How many apostles did Jesus solemnly appoint after spending an entire night on the mountain in prayer to God (Luke 6:12-16)?
option_a: Seventy (70)
option_b: Twelve (12)
option_c: Seven (7)
option_d: Three (3)
explanation: After praying all night, Jesus selected twelve apostles from His wider disciples, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel, to be with Him and preach.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Baptism, Temptation & Call of Disciples
question: Which three disciples formed the inner circle of Jesus' apostles, privileged to witness the raising of Jairus's daughter, the Transfiguration, and Gethsemane?
option_a: Andrew, Philip, and Thomas
option_b: Matthew, Simon the Zealot, and Judas
option_c: Peter, James, and John
option_d: Bartholomew, Jude, and James the Less
explanation: Peter, James, and John constituted the inner core witnessing pivotal moments of Christ's glory (Transfiguration) and agony (Gethsemane).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-12), what blessing is promised to the 'peacemakers'?
option_a: 'For they shall inherit the earth'
option_b: 'For they shall see God'
option_c: 'For they shall obtain mercy'
option_d: 'For they shall be called sons of God'
explanation: Matthew 5:9 declares: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus describes His disciples' influence in the world using which two vivid everyday metaphors (Matthew 5:13-16)?
option_a: Salt of the earth and Light of the world
option_b: Iron sword and Battle shield
option_c: Golden coins and Royal crowns
option_d: Desert wind and Ocean waves
explanation: Jesus taught: 'You are the salt of the earth' (preserving and flavoring society) and 'You are the light of the world' (shining good works before men).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: How did Jesus radicalize the Sixth Commandment ('You shall not murder') in Matthew 5:21-22?
option_a: By stating that soldiers are exempt from the commandment during war
option_b: By declaring that anyone who is angry with his brother or insults him is liable to judgment and the hell of fire
option_c: By commanding that murderers should be banished rather than executed
option_d: By requiring murderers to pay fifty talents of silver to the temple
explanation: Jesus internalized the Law: murder begins in the heart; harboring malicious anger or contemptuous insults ('Raca', 'You fool!') incurs severe moral guilt.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In Matthew 5:43-48, what radical ethical standard does Jesus mandate regarding personal enemies?
option_a: 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth'
option_b: 'Hate your enemies and destroy their crops at night'
option_c: 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven'
option_d: 'Report your enemies to the Roman governor for trial'
explanation: Rejecting vengeance, Jesus commanded boundless love: 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you', reflecting God who sends rain on just and unjust.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: What warning does Jesus give in Matthew 6 regarding the practice of piety (giving alms, praying, fasting)?
option_a: Blow trumpets in the streets so the community can praise your charity
option_b: Wear disfigured, mournful faces when fasting to prove your devotion
option_c: Pray only in the most crowded corners of municipal markets
option_d: Beware of practicing your piety before men in order to be seen by them; do it in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you
explanation: Jesus condemned hypocritical ostentation: religious devotion must be performed in secret before God, not as a theatrical display for human praise.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:3-23), what does the 'seed that fell on rocky ground' represent?
option_a: The person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy, but has no root, falling away when tribulation or persecution arises
option_b: The person who hears the word without understanding, from whom Satan snatches it away
option_c: The person whose word is choked by worldly cares and the delight in riches
option_d: The person who hears, understands, and bears fruit a hundredfold
explanation: Rocky ground represents superficial, shallow emotional conversion without deep root; when trials or persecutions arise, the faith immediately withers.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: What does the 'seed that fell among thorns' represent in the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:22)?
option_a: The hardened pathway trampled by commercial travelers
option_b: He who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the delight in riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful
option_c: The righteous disciple who gives away all his money to orphans
option_d: The false teacher who teaches pagan doctrines in synagogues
explanation: Thorns symbolize worldly anxieties and the deceitfulness of wealth, which choke spiritual life, preventing the word from bearing mature fruit.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32), how does the compassionate father receive his wayward, ruined younger son upon his return?
option_a: He ordered his servants to beat the boy with twenty stripes
option_b: He refused to open the front door until the son repaid all the squandered money
option_c: He saw him from afar, had compassion, ran, fell on his neck, kissed him, and clothed him with the best robe, ring, and shoes
option_d: He forced him to work as an unpaid bondservant in the pigsties
explanation: The father displayed unconditional grace: running to embrace his penitent son, restoring him to full sonship with the best robe, signet ring, and a fatted calf feast.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:29-37), who crossed the road and passed by the wounded traveler without helping him?
option_a: Two Roman soldiers
option_b: Two Samaritan merchants
option_c: A Pharisee and a tax collector
option_d: A Priest and a Levite
explanation: Both the Priest and the Levite (religious leaders) saw the wounded man and passed by on the other side, failing to show mercy.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: What defining question prompted Jesus to tell the Parable of the Good Samaritan?
option_a: 'And who is my neighbor?'
option_b: 'What must I do to inherit the wealth of Egypt?'
option_c: 'How many times shall my brother sin against me?'
option_d: 'Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar?'
explanation: A lawyer sought to justify himself by asking 'And who is my neighbor?'; Jesus illustrated that neighborliness is boundless, active compassion.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Weeds (Wheat and Tares, Matthew 13:24-30), why did the householder forbid his servants from pulling up the tares immediately?
option_a: Because the weeds were valuable for making pharmaceutical medicine
option_b: Lest in gathering the weeds they root up the wheat along with them; let both grow together until the harvest
option_c: Because the servants lacked iron scythes for weeding
option_d: Because the enemy was guarding the field with armed soldiers
explanation: The master commanded patience until the end-time harvest, preventing premature human judgment from accidentally destroying genuine wheat.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: What fatal mistake did the protagonist make in the Parable of the Rich Fool (Luke 12:16-21)?
option_a: He failed to pay statutory taxes to King Herod
option_b: He burned down his neighbor's vineyard in a dispute
option_c: He hoarded his bumper harvest in bigger barns, boasting in self-sufficiency ('eat, drink, be merry'), neglecting to be rich toward God
option_d: He refused to hire day laborers to reap his grain
explanation: The rich man lived for material accumulation and hedonistic ease, ignoring eternity; God said: 'Fool! This night your soul is required of you...'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what was the crime of the servant who received one talent?
option_a: He spent the talent on drunken partying with prostitutes
option_b: He was robbed by highway bandits on the road to Jericho
option_c: He loaned the money to the Roman military governor
option_d: He acted out of fear and sloth, burying his master's money in the ground rather than investing it to yield fruit
explanation: The one-talent servant was condemned as wicked and slothful because he buried the deposit out of fearful laziness, failing to put it to work.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector (Luke 18:9-14), why did the tax collector go home justified rather than the Pharisee?
option_a: Because he humbled himself, beating his breast and praying: 'God, be merciful to me a sinner!' while the Pharisee self-righteously boasted of his works
option_b: Because the tax collector paid double tithes to the temple treasury
option_c: Because the Pharisee was caught stealing money from the poor box
option_d: Because the tax collector was a close relative of the high priest
explanation: Jesus taught: 'Every one who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted'; true justification comes through humble repentance.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings: Sermon on the Mount & Parables
question: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard (Matthew 20:1-16), what principle of the Kingdom of God is illustrated when all workers receive the same wage?
option_a: The economic theory of collective communist agricultural wages
option_b: God's sovereign grace and generous mercy, which does not depend on human merit or seniority ('the last will be first, and the first last')
option_c: The unfairness of private vineyard owners in Judea
option_d: The requirement for trade unions to negotiate minimum wages
explanation: The landowner gives the 11th-hour workers the full denarius, demonstrating that entrance and rewards in the Kingdom rest on divine sovereign generosity, not human bargaining.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: What was the very first recorded miracle ('sign') performed by Jesus in His public ministry (John 2:1-11)?
option_a: Feeding five thousand men in the desert wilderness
option_b: Walking on the stormy waters of the Sea of Galilee
option_c: Turning water into wine at the wedding feast in Cana of Galilee
option_d: Healing a man born blind at the Pool of Siloam
explanation: At the wedding in Cana, Jesus turned six stone jars of water into choice wine, manifesting His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How was the woman who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve years healed in Luke 8:43-48?
option_a: She drank water from the Pool of Bethesda
option_b: Jesus laid His hands on her head in the synagogue
option_c: Peter prayed a prayer of healing over her in her house
option_d: She came up behind Jesus in faith and touched the fringe of His garment, and immediately her flow of blood dried up
explanation: Having spent all her living on physicians to no avail, she touched the hem of Jesus' garment in faith; Jesus sensed power go out from Him, confirming her healing.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How did Jesus heal the paralytic who was lowered through the roof by his four faithful friends at Capernaum (Mark 2:1-12)?
option_a: He first forgave the man's sins, then commanded: 'Rise, take up your pallet and go home'
option_b: He bathed the man's paralyzed limbs in olive oil
option_c: He ordered the Roman centurion to carry the man to the hospital
option_d: He rebuked the Pharisees and struck them with paralysis
explanation: Seeing their faith, Jesus declared 'Son, your sins are forgiven', and proved His divine authority to forgive sins by healing the paralytic physically.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How did Jesus calm the terrifying gale of wind on the Sea of Galilee when His disciples panicked in fear (Mark 4:35-41)?
option_a: He ordered the disciples to throw the cargo overboard
option_b: He awoke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea: 'Peace! Be still!' and there was a great calm
option_c: He commanded Peter to jump into the water and pull the boat
option_d: He blew on a silver trumpet from the stern of the boat
explanation: Jesus demonstrated sovereign authority over nature: He rebuked the tempestuous wind and sea with 'Peace! Be still!', prompting awe: 'Who then is this, that even wind and sea obey him?'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: What small food provision did Jesus miraculously multiply to feed five thousand men besides women and children (Matthew 14:13-21)?
option_a: Seven loaves of wheat bread and three small fish
option_b: Twelve baskets of dried figs and honey cakes
option_c: Five loaves of barley bread and two fish
option_d: Two roasted quails and one bowl of olive oil
explanation: From a boy's lunch of five barley loaves and two fish, Jesus gave thanks, broke, and distributed the food, feeding 5,000+ with 12 baskets of fragments left over.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: What miracle took place in the fourth watch of the night while the disciples' boat was battered by waves on the Sea of Galilee (Matthew 14:22-33)?
option_a: An angel flew down and carried the boat to the opposite shore
option_b: The waters of the sea split into two dry pathways
option_c: A giant whale carried the disciples to Capernaum
option_d: Jesus came to them walking on the water, and Peter briefly walked on the water toward Him in faith
explanation: Jesus walked upon the stormy sea; Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on water until distracted by the fierce wind, crying 'Lord, save me!'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: In Luke 7:11-17, what dead person did Jesus raise to life outside the city gate of Nain?
option_a: The only son of a weeping widow, whose funeral procession was heading to the burial ground
option_b: The daughter of Jairus, ruler of the synagogue
option_c: Lazarus, brother of Mary and Martha
option_d: A Roman soldier who died of desert fever
explanation: Moved with deep compassion for the grieving widow, Jesus touched the funeral bier and said: 'Young man, I say to you, arise', restoring him alive to his mother.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How did Jesus raise the twelve-year-old daughter of Jairus from the dead in Mark 5:35-43?
option_a: He sprinkled holy water on her forehead three times
option_b: He took her by the hand and commanded: 'Talitha cumi' (Little girl, I say to you, arise)
option_c: He breathed into her nostrils the breath of life
option_d: He commanded Peter to lay his walking staff on her body
explanation: Dismissing the mockers, Jesus took the girl by the hand and spoke in Aramaic: 'Talitha cumi' ('Little girl, arise'); she immediately stood up and walked.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: In John 11, for how many days had Lazarus of Bethany been dead and buried in the tomb before Jesus raised him?
option_a: One day
option_b: Seven days
option_c: Four days (he was already decomposing and smelled)
option_d: Twelve hours
explanation: Martha objected that Lazarus had been dead four days and would stink; Jesus prayed and called with a loud voice: 'Lazarus, come out!', raising him.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How did Jesus deliver the fierce demon-possessed man who lived among the tombs in the country of the Gerasenes (Mark 5:1-20)?
option_a: He tied the man with heavy iron chains to a tree
option_b: He commanded the Roman garrison to banish the man to Damascus
option_c: He struck the demoniac with physical muteness
option_d: He cast out the legion of unclean spirits, permitting them to enter a herd of two thousand swine that rushed into the sea and drowned
explanation: Jesus expelled the 'Legion' of demons into a herd of swine, restoring the man to his right mind, sitting clothed at Jesus' feet.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: How was the blind beggar Bartimaeus healed near the gates of Jericho in Mark 10:46-52?
option_a: He cried persistently: 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' and Jesus said: 'Go your way; your faith has made you well'
option_b: Jesus made clay with spittle and anointed his eyes
option_c: The disciples washed Bartimaeus in the river Jordan
option_d: Bartimaeus paid two copper coins to the temple treasury
explanation: Bartimaeus refused to be silenced, crying out to the 'Son of David'; Jesus responded to his persistent faith, instantly restoring his sight.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Miracles of Jesus (Healing, Nature, Resurrection of Dead)
question: When Jesus healed ten lepers on the way to Jerusalem in Luke 17:11-19, how many returned to praise God and give thanks at Jesus' feet?
option_a: All ten men returned dancing with joy
option_b: Only one (and he was a Samaritan foreigner)
option_c: Five returned while five went to the priests
option_d: None returned because they forgot
explanation: Only one of the ten cleansed lepers returned to fall at Jesus' feet giving thanks, and he was an outsider (Samaritan); Jesus asked: 'Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine?'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In Matthew 18:21-22, what answer did Jesus give when Peter asked: 'Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? As many as seven times?'
option_a: 'Three times only, and thereafter report him to the court'
option_b: 'Until he repays every copper coin he owes you'
option_c: 'I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven'
option_d: 'Only once, for a righteous man never sins twice'
explanation: Jesus shattered legalistic limits on forgiveness: 'seventy times seven' (490 times) signifies infinite, boundless, and continuous forgiveness.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant (Matthew 18:23-35), why was the servant handed over to the jailers to be tortured?
option_a: Because he stole golden vessels from the king's palace
option_b: Because he failed to pay his annual military service tax
option_c: Because he refused to attend the king's wedding banquet
option_d: Because after his master forgave him a massive debt of 10,000 talents, he choked a fellow servant who owed him a tiny debt of 100 denarii and threw him in prison
explanation: Having received mercy for an unpayable debt (10,000 talents), the servant ruthlessly imprisoned a peer over a pittance (100 denarii), earning severe condemnation.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9-13; Luke 11:2-4), what petition directly ties our forgiveness from God to our forgiveness of others?
option_a: 'And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors'
option_b: 'Give us this day our daily bread'
option_c: 'Hallowed be thy name'
option_d: 'Deliver us from evil'
explanation: Jesus taught that experiencing divine pardon requires a forgiving heart: 'forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What lesson on persistence in prayer did Jesus teach through the Parable of the Persistent Widow and the Unjust Judge (Luke 18:1-8)?
option_a: Judges are universally corrupt and should be avoided
option_b: Men ought always to pray and not lose heart, for God will vindicate His elect who cry to Him day and night
option_c: Widows should hire professional lawyers to litigate disputes
option_d: Prayer is effective only when recited in Hebrew
explanation: Jesus told the parable to show that disciples must pray continuously without giving up; if an unjust judge relents to persistence, how much more will a loving God answer His children.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What does the Parable of the Friend at Midnight (Luke 11:5-8) teach concerning prayer?
option_a: One must never wake up neighbors during the night
option_b: Bread should always be baked three days in advance
option_c: Bold persistence (importunity) in prayer: ask and it will be given, seek and you will find, knock and it will be opened
option_d: Hospitality is unnecessary after midnight
explanation: Because of the friend's shameless persistence, the neighbor gets up and gives him bread; Jesus applies this: 'Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find...'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In Matthew 6:6, what instructions does Jesus give regarding personal private prayer?
option_a: 'Stand at the street corners where everyone can admire your piety'
option_b: 'Use vain, endless repetitions like the pagans do'
option_c: 'Shout with a loud voice so heaven can hear your words'
option_d: 'When you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you'
explanation: Jesus directed believers to pray in the private inner closet without empty repetitive babbling, communing sincerely with the Father who knows our needs.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31-32), what reality of the Kingdom of God is illustrated?
option_a: The Kingdom starts from tiny, insignificant beginnings but grows into immense, expansive greatness that shelters all nations
option_b: The Kingdom of God can only be found in agricultural vegetable gardens
option_c: Mustard seeds possess supernatural magical medicinal powers
option_d: Only small children will be allowed into the Kingdom of God
explanation: The mustard seed is the smallest of garden seeds, yet grows into a large tree where birds lodge, illustrating the Kingdom's tiny start and vast global growth.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In the Parable of the Leaven (Yeast, Matthew 13:33), how does the Kingdom of God work within human society?
option_a: Through violent military conquest and armed revolution
option_b: Silently, invisibly, and permeating from within until the entire lump of dough is transformed
option_c: By imposing legal penalties on non-believers
option_d: By establishing commercial bakery monopolies in cities
explanation: Leaven works unseen from within, steadily transforming the entire mass of flour, mirroring the quiet, pervasive, transforming power of the Kingdom.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What do the twin parables of the Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Value (Matthew 13:44-46) teach about the Kingdom of God?
option_a: True believers should search for buried gold in ancient cemeteries
option_b: Merchants make the most righteous disciples of Christ
option_c: The Kingdom of God is of supreme, incomparable worth, justifying joyful sacrifice of all worldly possessions to obtain it
option_d: Wealthy citizens can buy their salvation with pearls
explanation: Both the treasure in the field and the pearl of great price represent the supreme value of the Kingdom, prompting individuals to gladly sell all to possess it.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: In Matthew 18:1-4, who did Jesus present as the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?
option_a: The high priest who offers incense in the holy of holies
option_b: The wealthiest merchant who gives large alms
option_c: The fiercest warrior who defeats Roman legionaries
option_d: Whoever humbles himself like a little child
explanation: Jesus called a child into their midst, teaching that greatness in the Kingdom requires childlike humility, trust, and unpretentious simplicity.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What did Jesus declare regarding the difficulty of wealthy people entering the Kingdom of God (Matthew 19:23-24)?
option_a: 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God'
option_b: 'Rich people are permanently barred from eternal life under all circumstances'
option_c: 'Wealthy citizens must surrender all their money to Roman tax collectors'
option_d: 'Only impoverished beggars are permitted to hear the Gospel'
explanation: Jesus used hyperbole ('camel through the eye of a needle') to emphasize how riches foster pride and false security, though 'with God all things are possible'.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What does Jesus teach concerning material anxiety, food, and clothing in Matthew 6:25-34?
option_a: 'Store up food in underground silos for seventy years'
option_b: 'Do not be anxious about your life... Look at the birds of the air... Consider the lilies of the field... seek first his kingdom and his righteousness'
option_c: 'Weave your own clothing using expensive Egyptian linen'
option_d: 'Spend all your time calculating tomorrow's market inflation'
explanation: Jesus forbids crippling anxiety: our heavenly Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies, so believers must prioritize God's Kingdom, trusting His daily provision.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: When the Pharisees asked when the Kingdom of God was coming in Luke 17:20-21, how did Jesus reply?
option_a: 'It will arrive when an eclipse darkens the city of Rome'
option_b: 'It will appear with an army of golden flying horses'
option_c: 'The kingdom of God is not coming with signs to be observed... for behold, the kingdom of God is in the midst of you (within you)'
option_d: 'It will be established in the year that the Temple is destroyed'
explanation: The Kingdom is not a worldly political empire with physical borders; it is present spiritually wherever Christ reigns in the hearts of men.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Life and Teachings of Jesus Christ
topic: Teachings on Forgiveness, Prayer & the Kingdom of God
question: What warning did Jesus issue in Matthew 7:1-5 regarding judging others?
option_a: 'Always report your neighbor's sins to the Roman governor'
option_b: 'Judges must execute all petty thieves without hearing witnesses'
option_c: 'Righteous men are commanded to condemn all sinners publicly'
option_d: 'Judge not, that you be not judged... Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?'
explanation: Jesus condemned hypocritical, censorious fault-finding: we must examine our own massive flaws ('log') before arrogantly criticizing another's small fault ('speck').
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: At the Last Supper (Matthew 26:26-28), what symbolic meaning did Jesus give to the Bread and the Cup?
option_a: The bread represented His body given for them, and the cup represented His blood of the new covenant poured out for the forgiveness of sins
option_b: The bread represented the manna of Moses, and the cup represented the bitter waters of Marah
option_c: The bread represented the wealth of Egypt, and the cup represented the river Nile
option_d: The bread represented the Roman Empire, and the cup represented Caesar's taxes
explanation: Jesus instituted the Holy Communion (Eucharist), identifying the broken bread with His sacrificial body and the cup of wine with His covenant blood shed for sins.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: How did Jesus demonstrate humble servant leadership to His disciples on the evening of the Last Supper in John 13:1-17?
option_a: He presented each disciple with a gold signet ring
option_b: He poured water into a basin and washed His disciples' feet, wiping them with a towel
option_c: He commanded Peter to anoint Him with costly nard
option_d: He ordered the disciples to bow down before His throne
explanation: Jesus performed the menial duty of a household slave by washing their feet, giving an example: 'If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: What was the agonizing prayer Jesus offered three times in the Garden of Gethsemane as His sweat became like great drops of blood (Luke 22:42)?
option_a: 'Father, strike Judas Iscariot with lightning before he reaches the garden'
option_b: 'Father, send twelve legions of angels to destroy the Sanhedrin'
option_c: 'Father, if thou art willing, remove this cup from me; nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done'
option_d: 'Father, let me return to Nazareth to live as a carpenter'
explanation: Facing the horror of bearing the sin of the world, Jesus demonstrated ultimate filial surrender: 'not my will, but thine, be done' (Luke 22:42).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: With what pre-arranged sign did Judas Iscariot betray Jesus to the armed crowd in Gethsemane (Matthew 26:48-49)?
option_a: By pointing an iron spear at Jesus
option_b: By tearing his own outer garment
option_c: By throwing thirty pieces of silver on the ground
option_d: With a kiss ('Hail, Master!')
explanation: Judas gave the temple cohort a hypocritical sign of affection: 'The one I shall kiss is the man; seize him.' Greeting Jesus, he kissed Him.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: What violent act did Simon Peter commit during the arrest of Jesus in Gethsemane, and how did Jesus respond (John 18:10-11; Luke 22:50-51)?
option_a: Peter drew a sword and cut off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's slave; Jesus touched his ear and healed him, commanding Peter to put up his sword
option_b: Peter threw stones at the Roman soldiers and fled into the hills
option_c: Peter challenged Judas to a wrestling match
option_d: Peter set fire to the olive trees in the garden
explanation: Peter slashed off Malchus's ear; Jesus commanded him to put away the sword ('for all who take the sword will perish by the sword') and healed the man.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: During His trial before the Jewish Sanhedrin presided over by High Priest Caiaphas, what charge of 'blasphemy' was leveled against Jesus (Matthew 26:63-65)?
option_a: He claimed that He would overthrow the Roman emperor Caesar
option_b: He affirmed under solemn oath that He was the Christ, the Son of God, who would be seen seated at the right hand of Power
option_c: He admitted that He had stolen gold from the temple treasury
option_d: He refused to observe the Jewish Passover feast
explanation: When Caiaphas adjured Him by the living God, Jesus affirmed He was the Christ and would sit at God's right hand; Caiaphas tore his robes, crying: 'He has blasphemed!'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: How did Simon Peter fulfill Jesus' prophecy during the night of the trials in the courtyard of the high priest (Matthew 26:69-75)?
option_a: He confessed boldly before Caiaphas and was imprisoned
option_b: He paid thirty pieces of silver to bribe the prison guards
option_c: He denied three times that he knew Jesus, after which the rooster crowed, and Peter went out and wept bitterly
option_d: He escaped across the Jordan River on a camel
explanation: Warming himself at the fire, Peter denied knowing Jesus three times; when the rooster crowed, he remembered Jesus' words and wept bitterly in broken repentance.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: What happened to the remorseful Judas Iscariot after realizing that Jesus had been condemned to death (Matthew 27:3-5)?
option_a: He asked Peter for forgiveness and joined the disciples in Galilee
option_b: He purchased a merchant ship and sailed to Rome
option_c: He was executed by the Roman governor Pontius Pilate
option_d: He threw the thirty pieces of silver into the sanctuary, departed, and went and hanged himself
explanation: Overcome with despair, Judas cast down the blood money in the temple and hanged himself (the priests used the money to purchase the Potter's Field, Akeldama).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: What criminal was released by Pontius Pilate instead of Jesus due to the clamor of the crowd incited by the chief priests (Mark 15:6-15)?
option_a: Barabbas, who was in prison with rebels who had committed murder in the insurrection
option_b: Dathan
option_c: Simon the sorcerer
option_d: Barnabas
explanation: Pilate offered to release Jesus under the Passover custom, but the crowd shouted for Barabbas (a violent insurrectionist and murderer) to be released instead.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Last Supper, Arrest & Trials of Jesus
question: What symbolic act did Pontius Pilate perform before the roaring multitude when sentencing Jesus to be crucified (Matthew 27:24)?
option_a: He broke his official Roman wooden rod of office
option_b: He took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying: 'I am innocent of this man's blood; see to it yourselves'
option_c: He tore his official purple governor's toga
option_d: He burned the legal indictment scroll on the judgment seat
explanation: Knowing Jesus was innocent and delivered out of envy, Pilate washed his hands to evade moral responsibility, yielding to political blackmail.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: Who was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry the heavy cross of Jesus to Golgotha (Mark 15:21)?
option_a: Joseph of Arimathea
option_b: Nicodemus
option_c: Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus
option_d: Barnabas of Cyprus
explanation: Simon of Cyrene (an African from modern Libya) was conscripted by Roman soldiers to bear Christ's cross along the Via Dolorosa to Golgotha.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What is the meaning of the Aramaic name 'Golgotha' (Calvary), the site of the crucifixion (Matthew 27:33)?
option_a: The Mount of Olives
option_b: The Valley of Judgment
option_c: The High Hill of Kings
option_d: The Place of a Skull
explanation: Golgotha translates as 'the Place of a Skull' (in Latin, Calvaria), a rocky hill outside the walls of Jerusalem.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What inscription did Pontius Pilate write and put on the cross above Jesus' head in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek (John 19:19)?
option_a: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS' (INRI)
option_b: 'A REBEL AGAINST THE ROMAN EMPIRE'
option_c: 'THE BLASPHEMOUS PROPHET OF GALILEE'
option_d: 'A MAN CONDEMNED TO DEATH BY THE JEWISH COUNCIL'
explanation: Pilate wrote the charge in the three major languages of the Mediterranean world: 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews', refusing the chief priests' demand to alter it.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What divine plea of forgiveness did Jesus utter from the cross for His executioners (Luke 23:34)?
option_a: 'Father, strike Rome with ten plagues'
option_b: 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do'
option_c: 'Father, call down fire from heaven to consume them'
option_d: 'Father, why hast thou forgotten my tears?'
explanation: In supreme compassion, Jesus prayed for the Roman soldiers and Jewish rulers: 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do' (Luke 23:34).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What promise did Jesus make to the penitent thief crucified beside Him who prayed: 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom' (Luke 23:42-43)?
option_a: 'You must wait seventy years in purgatory'
option_b: 'If you climb down from your cross you shall be saved'
option_c: 'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise'
option_d: 'Your good works on earth will be weighed in the balance'
explanation: Jesus rewarded the dying thief's faith: 'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: At the ninth hour (about 3:00 PM), what anguished cry did Jesus utter on the cross in Aramaic (Matthew 27:46)?
option_a: 'Talitha cumi'
option_b: 'Ephphatha'
option_c: 'Maranatha'
option_d: 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' ('My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?')
explanation: Quoting Psalm 22:1, Jesus cried: 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?', expressing the agony of bearing divine wrath for the sins of the world as the Father turned His face away.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What were the triumphant final words uttered by Jesus just before He died on the cross (John 19:30; Luke 23:46)?
option_a: 'It is finished!' and 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!'
option_b: 'The battle is lost and darkness triumphs'
option_c: 'Rome shall pay for my blood'
option_d: 'Let the disciples scatter into the hills'
explanation: 'Tetelestai' ('It is finished!') declared the completion of redemption; He then breathed His last: 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What dramatic supernatural event occurred in the Temple at the exact moment of Jesus' death (Matthew 27:51)?
option_a: The golden candlestick (Menorah) was extinguished by a whirlwind
option_b: The curtain (veil) of the Temple was torn in two, from top to bottom
option_c: The altar of incense collapsed into dust
option_d: The roof of the temple caught fire
explanation: The tearing of the thick temple veil from top to bottom signified that Christ's death opened direct access into the Holy of Holies for all believers (Hebrews 10:19-20).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: What testimony did the Roman centurion standing opposite the cross make when he saw how Jesus died (Mark 15:39)?
option_a: 'Caesar is the only true god of Rome'
option_b: 'This man was an innocent Galilean prophet'
option_c: 'Truly this man was the Son of God!'
option_d: 'The Jewish leaders were right to condemn him'
explanation: Witnessing the earthquake, darkness, and Christ's majestic death, the hardened Roman commander confessed: 'Truly this man was the Son of God!'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Crucifixion, Death & Burial of Jesus
question: Who went boldly to Pontius Pilate to request the body of Jesus and buried Him in his own new rock-hewn tomb (Matthew 27:57-60)?
option_a: Simon Peter
option_b: John the beloved disciple
option_c: Lazarus of Bethany
option_d: Joseph of Arimathea (assisted by Nicodemus)
explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy counselor and secret disciple, obtained Pilate's permission and wrapped Jesus' body in clean linen, laying Him in his new rock tomb.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: Who were the first witnesses to discover the empty tomb on the first day of the week (Sunday morning) in Matthew 28:1-8 and John 20:1-2?
option_a: Mary Magdalene and the other women (Mary the mother of James, Salome)
option_b: Peter and John exclusively
option_c: The Roman soldiers guarding the gates
option_d: Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea
explanation: Early on Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene and the women arrived with spices to anoint the body, discovering the stone rolled away and the tomb empty.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: What glorious message did the angel at the empty tomb deliver to the terrified women in Matthew 28:5-6?
option_a: 'Why have you disturbed the sleep of the dead?'
option_b: 'Do not be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay'
option_c: 'The disciples have stolen his body away in the night'
option_d: 'Go to Rome and report to Caesar Augustus'
explanation: The angel proclaimed the core truth of the Christian faith: 'He is not here; for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: To whom did the risen Christ first appear personally outside the empty tomb in John 20:11-18?
option_a: Simon Peter
option_b: His mother Mary
option_c: Mary Magdalene
option_d: Cleopas on the road to Emmaus
explanation: Jesus first revealed Himself to weeping Mary Magdalene, commissioning her as the 'apostle to the apostles' to announce His resurrection to the brethren.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: On the afternoon of the resurrection, how did the two disciples traveling on the road to Emmaus finally recognize the risen Jesus (Luke 24:13-35)?
option_a: When He showed them the scar on His forehead
option_b: When He performed a miracle of turning water into wine
option_c: When He spoke in foreign Greek tongues
option_d: When He sat at table with them, took the bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them
explanation: Their eyes were opened and they recognized Him in the breaking of the bread, recalling how their hearts burned within them as He opened the Scriptures.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: What did the apostle Thomas declare when the other disciples told him they had seen the risen Lord in John 20:24-25?
option_a: 'Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, and place my finger in the mark of the nails, and place my hand into his side, I will not believe'
option_b: 'Praise be to the God of Abraham who has conquered death'
option_c: 'I shall travel to Galilee immediately to meet Him'
option_d: 'He must be an angelic spirit without flesh and bones'
explanation: 'Doubting Thomas' demanded tangible empirical proof: touching the nail marks and the spear wound in Christ's side before he would believe.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: What was Thomas's profound confession of faith when Jesus appeared eight days later and invited him to touch His wounds (John 20:26-29)?
option_a: 'Truly you are a great prophet of Israel'
option_b: 'My Lord and my God!'
option_c: 'Forgive my foolish carpentry doubts'
option_d: 'You are the king of the Roman empire'
explanation: Overcome with awe, Thomas confessed the full deity of Christ: 'My Lord and my God!' Jesus commended future believers who believe without physical sight.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: How did Jesus lovingly restore Simon Peter by the Sea of Tiberias after Peter's three denials (John 21:15-17)?
option_a: He ordered Peter to fast for forty days in the wilderness
option_b: He stripped Peter of his apostolic title and gave it to John
option_c: He asked Peter three times: 'Simon, son of John, do you love me?' and commanded him: 'Feed my sheep'
option_d: He commanded Peter to build a stone monument on the shore
explanation: Matching Peter's three denials, Jesus asked three times 'Do you love me?', reinstating and commissioning Peter to shepherd His flock.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: What is the 'Great Commission' given by the risen Christ to His disciples on the mountain in Galilee (Matthew 28:18-20)?
option_a: 'Stay inside the city of Jerusalem and build an armed defense tower'
option_b: 'Preach the Law of Moses exclusively to the circumcised Jews'
option_c: 'Collect monetary tithes from all Roman officials across Judea'
option_d: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you'
explanation: With all authority in heaven and on earth, Jesus commanded global discipleship, worldwide baptism, and obedience, promising: 'I am with you always, to the close of the age.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: From which location did Jesus ascend into heaven forty days after His resurrection (Acts 1:9-12; Luke 24:50-51)?
option_a: The Mount of Olives (near Bethany)
option_b: The summit of Mount Sinai
option_c: The courtyard of the Jerusalem Temple
option_d: The shore of the Sea of Galilee
explanation: Jesus led them out as far as Bethany on the Mount of Olives, blessed them, and was lifted up into heaven as a cloud received Him from their sight.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Resurrection & Ascension of Jesus
question: What comforting promise did the two men in white robes (angels) give to the disciples gazing up into heaven after the Ascension (Acts 1:11)?
option_a: 'Do not weep, for Christ has established His throne on Mount Hermon'
option_b: 'This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven'
option_c: 'You must elect a new high priest before sunset'
option_d: 'The kingdom of Rome will endure for a thousand years'
explanation: The angels promised the visible, glorious Second Coming: 'This Jesus... will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven' (Acts 1:11).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: What promise did Jesus command the disciples to wait for in Jerusalem before departing on their global mission (Acts 1:4-8)?
option_a: A military army sent from the king of Persia
option_b: A decree of religious freedom issued by the Roman senate
option_c: The promise of the Father: 'You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be my witnesses... to the end of the earth'
option_d: A treasure of gold coins discovered under the Temple altar
explanation: Jesus instructed them to wait in Jerusalem for the baptism of the Holy Spirit, who would empower them to be witnesses locally and globally.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: Who was chosen by casting lots in Acts 1:15-26 to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve Apostles?
option_a: Joseph Barsabbas (Justus)
option_b: Barnabas
option_c: Stephen
option_d: Matthias

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)

option_a: A sound like the rush of a violent wind from heaven, and divided tongues as of fire resting upon each of them

explanation: Acts 2:2-3 describes the auditory phenomenon (a sound like a mighty rushing wind) and visual manifestation (tongues of fire resting on each disciple).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: What miraculous ability did the disciples demonstrate immediately upon being filled with the Holy Spirit on Pentecost (Acts 2:4)?
option_a: They were able to physically fly above the rooftops of Jerusalem

option_c: They became invisible to the temple police officers
option_d: They spoke ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics without study
explanation: Filled with the Spirit, they spoke in diverse languages, enabling multinational Jewish pilgrims from Parthia, Medea, Egypt, and Rome to hear God's wonders in their own native tongues.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: How did skeptical mockers in the crowd attempt to explain the disciples speaking in other tongues on Pentecost (Acts 2:13)?

subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)

option_a: Malachi
option_b: Daniel

option_d: Joel ('And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh...')
explanation: Peter explained the event as the fulfillment of Joel 2:28-32: God pouring out His Spirit on all flesh, with sons and daughters prophesying.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: In his Pentecost sermon, what central truth did Peter boldly proclaim concerning the crucified and risen Jesus (Acts 2:36)?
option_a: 'Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified'
option_b: 'Jesus was merely an innocent martyr of Roman political tyranny'
option_c: 'Israel must crown an earthly descendant of David in Jerusalem'
option_d: 'The Temple sacrifices must be resumed with greater zeal'

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: When the crowd was 'cut to the heart' and cried 'Brethren, what shall we do?', what instruction did Peter give (Acts 2:37-38)?

explanation: Peter commanded repentance and baptism in the name of Jesus Christ for remission of sins, promising the gift of the Holy Spirit.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: How many souls gladly received the word, were baptized, and added to the Church on the Day of Pentecost (Acts 2:41)?
option_a: Five hundred souls

option_d: Five thousand souls
explanation: Acts 2:41 records that about three thousand souls received Peter's word, were baptized, and joined the apostolic church on that single day.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Pentecost & the Holy Spirit (Acts 1-2)
question: According to Acts 2:42, what were the four continuous spiritual pillars of the early Christian community?
option_a: Building stone cathedrals, electing bishops, military drills, and farming

option_c: Political campaigning, tax boycotts, street protests, and trade guilds

explanation: Acts 2:42 outlines the essential life of the church: 'And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.'
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: What miracle performed by Peter and John at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple sparked public astonishment and official arrest (Acts 3:1-10)?

option_b: The raising of the high priest's daughter from the dead

option_d: Striking the temple guards with physical blindness

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: What bold reply did Peter and John give when the Sanhedrin strictly commanded them never to speak or teach in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:18-20)?
option_a: 'We promise to obey your commands and preach only in secret'

explanation: The apostles prioritized divine obedience over human intimidation: 'We cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard' (Acts 4:20; 5:29).
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: What terrible judgment befell Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5:1-11 for lying to the Holy Spirit about their property sale?

option_c: They fell down dead immediately at Peter's feet and were buried
option_d: They were excommunicated and forced to pay a heavy fine
explanation: Ananias and Sapphira conspired to deceive the church by pretending they gave 100% of their property proceeds; both dropped dead for lying to the Holy Spirit.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: What wise advice did the respected Pharisee and doctor of the Law, Gamaliel, give to the Sanhedrin regarding the apostles (Acts 5:34-39)?
option_a: 'Execute all twelve apostles immediately in the public square'
option_b: 'Banish the Christians to the desert of Arabia'
option_c: 'Force them to pay double taxes to the temple treasury'
option_d: 'Keep away from these men and let them alone; for if this plan or this undertaking is of men, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them'
explanation: Gamaliel cited Theudas and Judas the Galilean, advising restraint: if of human origin it will collapse, but if of God, they might find themselves fighting God.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: Why were the Seven Deacons (including Stephen and Philip) appointed in Acts 6:1-6?
option_a: To oversee the daily distribution of food to Hellenist widows, freeing the apostles for prayer and the ministry of the word
option_b: To command armed security patrols guarding the house of Peter
option_c: To write the four Gospel manuscripts in Greek
option_d: To collect financial taxes from Roman soldiers
explanation: Complaints by Greek-speaking Jewish widows over food distribution prompted the appointment of seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and wisdom.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: Who became the first Christian martyr (protomartyr), stoned to death while praying for his executioners: 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' (Acts 7)?
option_a: James, son of Zebedee
option_b: Stephen
option_c: Barnabas

subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church

option_a: Nicodemus
option_b: Cornelius

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church

option_d: He explained the messianic prophecy of Isaiah 53 (the sheep led to slaughter), preached Jesus to him, and baptized him in water

subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: What revolutionary vision did Peter see on the rooftop at Joppa that prepared him to preach the Gospel to the Gentile Cornelius (Acts 10)?
option_a: A great sheet let down from heaven containing all kinds of four-footed animals, with a voice saying: 'What God has cleansed, you must not call common'
option_b: A golden chariot flying across the Mediterranean Sea
option_c: A vision of the burning bush on Mount Horeb
option_d: An angel commanding him to fast for forty days
explanation: God used the vision of clean and unclean animals to break Peter's Jewish dietary prejudice, revealing that Gentiles are fully acceptable to God through faith.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: The Early Church: Fellowship, Mission & Opposition (Acts 3-12)
question: How was Peter miraculously delivered from maximum-security prison on the night before King Herod Agrippa I planned to execute him (Acts 12:1-11)?
option_a: John and Mark bribed the Roman prison guards with silver

option_c: An earthquake shattered the prison walls in pieces
option_d: Cornelius led a company of centurions to break open the doors
explanation: While the church prayed earnestly, an angel entered, woke sleeping Peter, chains dropped from his hands, and the city's iron gate opened automatically.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel
question: What dramatic event brought about the radical conversion of Saul of Tarsus on the road to Damascus in Acts 9:1-9?
option_a: He was defeated in a theological debate by Stephen in Jerusalem

option_c: A sudden light from heaven flashed around him, he fell to the ground, and heard Jesus say: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?'
option_d: He was healed of physical leprosy by the apostle Peter
explanation: The glorified Christ confronted Saul directly on the Damascus road; blinded by the light, Saul surrendered: 'Who are you, Lord?' and was told to enter the city.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel
question: Which disciple in Damascus was commanded by the Lord in a vision to go to the street called Straight and lay hands on Saul to restore his sight (Acts 9:10-19)?
option_a: Barnabas
option_b: Silas

explanation: Ananias obeyed the divine command despite fearing Saul's violent reputation, laid hands on him, scales fell from Saul's eyes, and Saul was baptized.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel

option_a: Jerusalem

option_a: Whether Christians were permitted to serve in the Roman imperial army
option_b: Which language the four Gospels should be translated into

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church

subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel

option_a: The Macedonian Call (a man of Macedonia standing and pleading: 'Come over to Macedonia and help us')
option_b: An angel holding a burning torch above the Aegean Sea
option_c: A vision of the Roman Colosseum standing empty
option_d: A voice from heaven commanding him to sail to Athens
explanation: At Troas, Paul saw a night vision of a Macedonian man crying 'Come over to Macedonia and help us', leading to the planting of churches in Philippi and Thessalonica.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel

explanation: An earthquake shook the prison; the terrified jailer was stopped from suicide by Paul, asked 'What must I do to be saved?', and believed with his entire household.
subject: Christian Religious Studies

section: Passion, Resurrection and the Early Church
topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Spread of the Gospel
question: In Athens, on the Areopagus (Mars' Hill), how did Paul begin his brilliant philosophical sermon to the Stoic and Epicurean philosophers (Acts 17:22-31)?
option_a: By mocking their pagan marble statues as worthless rubble

topic: Paul's Epistles: Faith, Grace & Christian Living (Romans, Galatians, Corinthians)

option_a: 'The power of God for salvation to every one who has faith... for in it the righteousness of God is revealed through faith for faith; as it is written, He who through faith is righteous shall live'
option_b: A secret philosophical puzzle understood only by Roman intellectuals
option_c: A revised version of the civil legal codes of Julius Caesar
option_d: A set of dietary regulations governing meat sold in markets
explanation: Paul unashamedly declares that the Gospel is God's saving power, revealing divine righteousness received entirely through faith (quoting Habakkuk 2:4).

topic: Paul's Epistles: Faith, Grace & Christian Living (Romans, Galatians, Corinthians)

option_a: Righteousness is earned by scrupulous adherence to the Levitical food laws
